validationCommand: OMNI_FP8_KEEP_ON_MOVE=1 python -c "import torch; t=torch.zeros(1,dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn); assert t.to('xpu').to('cpu').to('xpu').device.type=='xpu'; print('FP8 XPU keep-on-move OK')"
knownIssues: ComfyUI's comfy/ops.py:_quantized_apply has a hardcoded XPU stopgap that DEQUANTIZES fp8->bf16 on EVERY device move (to dodge a QTensor.clone() segfault, issue #14514). That doubles weight memory on each offload, so a two-stage fp8 diffusion model (e.g. WAN2.2 HIGH/LOW) OOMs at the HIGH->LOW swap with 'could not create a primitive' / UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY -- even though each fp8 UNet is only ~14.5GB.

comfy_kitchen < 0.2.28 lacks a working native fp8 path; 0.2.8 also lacked TensorWiseINT8Layout. Upgrade the shared venv to >= 0.2.28 (native onednn_w8a16_fp8 GEMM via omni_xpu_kernel) BEFORE relying on native fp8.
'node registered' evidence is not sufficient -- fp8 can import fine and only OOM/segfault at first inference or at a model swap.

Confirmed live 2026-08-08 (task a35d64a4, Intel Arc B60, comfy_kitchen 0.2.28): clean A/B -- with OMNI_FP8_KEEP_ON_MOVE unset the swap dequantizes (14649MB freed) and OOMs; with OMNI_FP8_KEEP_ON_MOVE=1 the swap moves fp8 cheaply (2147MB freed, no dequant) and a full 720x1280 x 81-frame WAN2.2 video completes on one 30GB XPU with no OOM.

workarounds.action: Upgrade comfy_kitchen to >= 0.2.28 in the shared venv, then apply patches/xpu-fp8-keep-quantized-on-move.patch to comfy/ops.py and launch ComfyUI with OMNI_FP8_KEEP_ON_MOVE=1. This keeps fp8 QuantizedTensors AS fp8 across device moves (no dequant-to-bf16), so offload/swap is cheap and native fp8 stays native.
workarounds.rationale: Removes the memory-doubling dequant-on-move that is the actual OOM cause; comfy_kitchen 0.2.28 makes the QTensor .to() path (#14514) safe so skipping the stopgap no longer segfaults.
workarounds.tradeoff: Requires the comfy_kitchen upgrade + the ops.py patch on the target; harmless when the model isn't fp8 (env is only read inside the fp8 branch).

workarounds.action: Run heavy aux models sequentially on XPU and free them between stages (offload is now cheap): VLM/llama_cpp nodes with force_offload=True, CLIP/text-encoder device=default (XPU, NOT cpu), UNet loaders weight_dtype=default (native fp8). Leave VAE on XPU (no --cpu-vae) -- ComfyUI auto-falls-back to tiled decode if a full decode would OOM.
workarounds.rationale: With keep-on-move, XPU-resident + sequential-offload is both faster and fits; only one big model is resident at a time (VLM ~14GB -> free, TE ~6GB -> free, one fp8 UNet ~14.5GB, VAE ~0.5GB).
workarounds.tradeoff: None vs the old CPU-pinning; CPU execution of TE/VAE was a pre-patch crutch and is 10-100x slower for these ops.

workarounds.action: LAST RESORT only if the keep-on-move patch cannot be applied on the target: set CLIPLoader device=cpu via runtime-policy JSON to sidestep the fp8 TE segfault (slower first-prompt latency).
workarounds.rationale: Correct but slow fallback for environments stuck on old comfy_kitchen / unpatched ops.py.
workarounds.tradeoff: First-prompt latency up by seconds-to-tens-of-seconds; does not by itself fix a two-UNet swap OOM (that needs the keep-on-move patch).

validationEvidence: Live A/B on task a35d64a4 (172.16.124.12, Arc B60, comfy_kitchen 0.2.28): patch OFF -> dequant+OOM; patch ON -> full 720x1280 x 81-frame WAN2.2 video, ~15 min, no OOM.
retireCondition: ComfyUI removes the XPU fp8 dequant-on-move stopgap upstream (keeping fp8 on device moves by default), making OMNI_FP8_KEEP_ON_MOVE + this patch a no-op.
